newsitem.title: INDIA: India fines Morgan Stanley firm citing violations.
newsitem.headline: India fines Morgan Stanley firm citing violations.

text.p: Capital markets regulator, the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) on Monday said it slapped a penalty on Morgan Stanley Asset Management India Pvt Ltd for violating Indian mutual fund regulations.
SEBI said it was levying a penalty of 200,000 rupees on the Indian subsidiary of the U.S.-based investment bank.
"These violations were of the investment norms prescribed by SEBI in the mutual fund regulations," it said in a statement.
This included undertaking activity akin to an asset management company for clients other than the Morgan Stanley Mutual Fund without prior approval of SEBI, it said.
The statement said Morgan Stanley also exceeded the five percent investment ceiling norm in company stocks and failure to deliver securities sold in the market.

"Accordingly, the adjudicating officer has after considering (Morgan Stanley's) replies (to the charges), other submissions made by the fund and personal hearing has come to the conclusion that violations did take place..."

SEBI had appointed an adjudicating officer to look into the fund's operations following findings of an inspection carried out by independent auditors into its affairs and on the basis of the fund's annual report for 1995/96 (April-March)
Morgan Stanley operates a close-ended mutual fund which has been quoted below par.
